ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, within a $2\times 4$ square grid, line segments $AB$ and $CD$ intersect at point $E$. If the side length of each small square is 1, what is the length of $DE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: \textbf{Solution:} From the figure, we know: $BC \parallel AD$, $\therefore \triangle CBE \sim \triangle DAE$, $\therefore \frac{CB}{AD} = \frac{CE}{DE}$, $\because CB = \sqrt{2^2 + 2^2} = 2\sqrt{2}$, $AD = \sqrt{1^2 + 1^2} = \sqrt{2}$, $\therefore \frac{CE}{DE} = \frac{2}{1}$, $\because CD = \sqrt{1^2 + 2^2} = \sqrt{5}$, $\therefore DE = \boxed{\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}}$

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} From the figure, we know: $BC \parallel AD$, $\therefore \triangle CBE \sim \triangle DAE$, $\therefore \frac{CB}{AD} = \frac{CE}{DE}$, $\because CB = \sqrt{2^2 + 2^2} = 2\sqrt{2}$, $AD = \sqrt{1^2 + 1^2} = \sqrt{2}$, $\therefore \frac{CE}{DE} = \frac{2}{1}$, $\because CD = \sqrt{1^2 + 2^2} = \sqrt{5}$, $\therefore DE = \boxed{\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}}$
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
First describe the image: The figure is a rectangular grid of 2 columns and 4 rows composed of unit small squares. Point A is on the middle vertical line of the bottom side, point B is at the upper right corner, point C is on the middle horizontal line of the left boundary, and point D is on the right boundary and on the horizontal line one square above the bottom. Line segment AB and CD intersect internally at point E. According to the positions in the figure, CB and AD are both along the same diagonal direction, so CB ∥ AD.

Then reason: Because BE and AE are on the same straight line AB, CE and DE are on the same straight line CD, and CB ∥ AD, so ∠CBE = ∠DAE, ∠CEB = ∠DEA, thus △CBE ∼ △DAE. Therefore there is CB/AD = CE/DE. Calculating from the unit grid, CB = sqrt(2^2 + 2^2) = 2sqrt(2), AD = sqrt(1^2 + 1^2) = sqrt(2), so CE/DE = 2. That is, CE:DE = 2:1. Also CD = sqrt(2^2 + 1^2) = sqrt(5), and CD = CE + DE, divided according to the ratio 2:1 into three equal parts proportionally, so DE = (1/3)CD = sqrt(5)/3.
